app.name: Plaani Äri
app.tagline: Write a bank-ready business plan for an Estonian loan, step by step.

footer.disclaimer: This is a planning tool, not legal, tax or financial advice. Check important decisions with a professional.

home.title: Get your business plan ready for the bank
home.intro: Answer simple questions about your business. The app turns them into a clear plan that follows what Estonian banks expect.
home.feature1Text: Step-by-step questions, from your idea to collateral. AI helps you write clear text.
home.feature2Text: Three-year forecast, loan schedule and the key ratios banks check. Estonian taxes built in.
home.feature3Text: Before you go to the bank, an AI credit officer finds weak points and asks hard questions.
home.deleted: Your account and all your data have been deleted.

summary.title: Summary
summary.hint: A short overview: what you do, how much you want to borrow, and why the bank will get its money back. You write it last, but it comes first.

idea.title: Business idea
idea.hint: Your product or service, the problem it solves, and why now is the right time.

market.title: Market and competitors
market.hint: How big the market is, who your main competitors are, and why customers will choose you.

customers.title: Customers
customers.hint: Who buys from you, how many customers you expect, and any first customers or agreements you already have.

team.title: Team
team.hint: The owners and key people, their experience, and who does what.

marketing.title: Marketing and sales
marketing.hint: How customers find you, your prices, sales channels and marketing budget.

operations.title: Operations
operations.hint: Location, equipment, suppliers, and the licences and permits you need.

risks.title: Risks
risks.hint: The main risks and how you reduce each one. Banks value owners who have thought this through.

loan.title: Loan purpose and amount
loan.hint: What the money is for, how much you need, for how long, and how you plan to pay it back.

ownContribution.title: Own contribution
ownContribution.hint: How much of your own money goes into the project and where it comes from. Banks often ask for 10–30%.

collateral.title: Collateral
collateral.hint: What secures the loan: real estate, a personal guarantee, or a guarantee from EIS (Enterprise Estonia).

settings.title: Settings
settings.deleteText: This deletes your login and all your plans for good. It cannot be undone.
settings.deleteConfirm: I understand that everything will be deleted.
settings.deleteError: We could not delete your account. Please try again.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.draftNote: Draft. The details of who runs this service will be added before launch.
privacy.whatText: Your email address (to send you login links) and the business plans you write. We do not ask for your name, ID code, address or phone number.
privacy.whereText: In a database in the European Union (Frankfurt, Germany). The app runs on Vercel servers in Frankfurt. Only you can see your plans.
privacy.aiText: When you use the AI helper, the translation or the bank officer check, the text of your plan is sent to Anthropic, the company that provides the AI, in the USA. Your email is not sent. To keep costs under control, we count how many AI requests each account makes per day.
privacy.cookiesText: We use one cookie only: the login cookie that keeps you signed in. No advertising or tracking cookies.
privacy.deleteText: You can see and change your plans at any time, and delete your account and all your plans in Settings. If you think your data is misused, you can complain to the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate (www.aki.ee).

results.title: Results
results.dscrHint: Banks and EIS look for at least {minimum}.
results.incomeTaxesFie: Owner's taxes (social tax, income tax, pension)
results.cashflow: Cash flow in year 1, month by month
results.how1: Taxes and rates come from Estonian law and the Tax and Customs Board, checked on {date}.
results.how2: Wages: employer adds 33% social tax (at least on the monthly minimum for a full-time employee) and 0.8% unemployment insurance. Payroll taxes and VAT are paid the next month.
results.how3: OÜ: profit kept in the company is not taxed. A dividend costs 22/78 of its amount in tax.
results.how4: FIE: social tax, income tax and pension are worked out per calendar year and paid as the law sets (quarterly advances, the rest on 1 October of the next year).
results.how5: DSCR = (EBITDA − income taxes − FIE owner's drawings) ÷ (loan principal + interest paid in the year). Purchases are assumed to carry 24% VAT.

explain.title: How the numbers are calculated
explain.intro: Open a topic to see each step with your own numbers and the Estonian rules used.
explain.note: Rounded to cents. This is a planning tool, not tax or legal advice. Check the rules with the Tax and Customs Board (EMTA) or an accountant before important decisions.

topics.payroll: Wage and taxes for one person a month

steps.payGross: Gross wage in the first month: {gross}.
steps.payMinimumBase: The wage is below the social tax monthly base of {minBase}. For a full-time employee the employer pays social tax on at least this amount.
steps.payNoUnemployment: A board member fee has no unemployment insurance and no minimum social tax.
steps.payEmployerCost: Cost to the business: {gross} + {socialTax} + {unemployment} = {cost} a month.
steps.payUnemploymentEmployee: Withheld from the wage: unemployment insurance {rate} × {gross} = {amount}.
steps.payPension: Withheld from the wage: funded pension (II pillar) {rate} × {gross} = {amount}.
steps.payTaxable: Income tax is counted from {gross} − {unemployment} − {pension} − tax-free income {exemption} = {taxable} (assuming the person uses the tax-free income at this job).
steps.payNet: Paid to the person (net wage): {net}. The employer pays the withheld amounts and its own taxes to the Tax and Customs Board by day {day} of the next month.
steps.loanRate: Interest {annual} a year is {monthly} a month.
steps.loanGrace: Interest-only months at the start: {months}. Interest {interest} a month.
steps.loanAnnuity: Equal monthly payments (annuity): the bank spreads {amount} plus interest evenly over {months} months, so each payment is {payment}. Formula: amount × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate)^−months).
steps.loanEqualPrincipal: Equal principal: each month you repay {amount} ÷ {months} = {principal} of the loan, plus interest on what is left, so the payments get smaller.
steps.loanFirst: First repayment {payment}: interest {monthly} × {balance} = {interest}, and {principal} pays back the loan.
steps.loanFee: Contract fee: {rate} × {amount} = {fee}, paid when the loan is paid out.
steps.vatRates: Your sales carry the VAT rate you chose for each product. Purchases and investments are counted with the standard rate of {rate}.
steps.vatSales: VAT you add to your sales in year 1: {amount}.
steps.vatPurchases: VAT on your purchases and investments that you can deduct: {amount}.
steps.vatToPay: VAT to pay to the Tax and Customs Board: {sales} − {purchases} = {net}. VAT is not your income or cost: you collect it for the state.
steps.vatRefund: VAT to get back from the Tax and Customs Board: {purchases} − {sales} = {net}.
steps.vatWhen: The VAT return is due by day {day} of the next month. The calculator assumes the payment (or refund) happens in that month.
steps.vatNotRegistered: You are not registered for VAT: you add no VAT to your sales, and the VAT you pay on purchases ({rate}) is part of your costs.
steps.vatThreshold: You must register when your taxable sales in a calendar year go above {threshold}.
steps.divNone: You plan no dividends, so the company pays no income tax. In Estonia, profit that stays in the company is not taxed.
steps.divTax: Dividend in year {year}: {dividend}. The company pays income tax {dividend} ÷ {divisor} × {rate} = {tax} (the 22/78 rule).
steps.divRetained: Profit that stays in the company is not taxed. Tax is paid only when profit is paid out.
steps.divOwner: An owner who lives in Estonia pays no extra income tax on this dividend.
steps.fieProfit: Business profit in {year} ({months} months in the forecast): {profit}.
steps.fieSocialTax: Social tax: {profit} ÷ {divisor} × {rate} = {amount}. Dividing by {divisor} takes the social tax itself out of the base.
steps.fieSocialTaxMinimum: That is below the minimum social tax for {months} months, {minimum}, so the minimum is paid.
steps.fieSocialTaxMaximum: That is above the maximum social tax, {maximum}, so the maximum is paid.
steps.fieTotal: Owner's taxes for the year in total: {total}.
steps.fieWhen: When they are paid: the minimum social tax every quarter, income tax advances from the second year, and the rest by 1 October of the next year.
steps.depCostWithVat: Purchase price {amount} plus VAT {rate} = {cost}. You are not registered for VAT, so the VAT is part of the cost.
steps.depPerYear: Written off evenly over the years of use: {cost} ÷ {years} = {perYear} a year ({perMonth} a month).
steps.depMeaning: Depreciation spreads the purchase over its useful life. It lowers the profit each year, but no money leaves the bank account then: you paid when you bought it.
steps.dscrEbitda: Operating profit before depreciation (EBITDA) in year {year}: {ebitda}.
steps.dscrAvailable: Money left to pay the loan: {available}.
steps.dscrDebtService: Loan payments in the year: principal {principal} + interest {interest} = {service}.
steps.dscrResult: DSCR = {available} ÷ {service} = {dscr}. Banks and EIS look for at least {minimum}.
steps.dscrMeaning: In plain words: for every 1 € of loan payment, the business earns {dscr} €.
steps.beFixed: Costs that do not depend on sales in year {year}: running costs {operating} + wages {wages} + employer taxes {employerTaxes} + depreciation {depreciation} + interest and fees {interest} = {fixed}.
steps.beMargin: Of each 1 € of sales, {margin} is left after goods and materials ({grossProfit} ÷ {revenue}).
steps.beResult: Break-even sales = {fixed} ÷ {margin} = {breakEven} a year. Above this the business makes a profit. Your plan: {revenue}.
steps.eqEquity: Equity at the end of year {year}: own money {own} + profit so far {profit} − paid to the owner {paid} = {equity}.
steps.eqResult: Equity share = {equity} ÷ total assets {assets} = {ratio}. EIS looks for at least {minimum}.
steps.crAssets: Current assets at the end of year {year}: cash {cash} + money owed by customers {receivables} + tax refund due {taxReceivable} = {total}.
steps.crLiabilities: Debts due within a year: taxes owed {taxPayable} + loan due within 12 months {loanCurrent} = {total}.
steps.crResult: Current ratio = {assets} ÷ {liabilities} = {ratio}. EIS looks for at least {minimum}. Above 1 means this year's debts can be paid from money you have or will soon receive.

whatYouDo.label: In one or two sentences: what does your business do and for whom?
whatYouDo.example: e.g. A café in Tartu city centre serving coffee and light lunches to students and office workers.

whyBank.label: Why should the bank believe the loan will be paid back?
whyBank.example: e.g. 5 years in the café business, signed lease, own money 30% of the project, steady lunch customers.

product.label: What do you sell? Describe your product or service.
product.example: e.g. Coffee, pastries baked on site, lunch menu, catering for small offices.

problem.label: What need or problem does it solve for customers?
problem.example: e.g. There is no café with quick lunches near the university campus.

whyNow.label: Why is now a good time to start or grow?
whyNow.example: e.g. A new office building with 400 workers opens next door in spring.

stage.label: How far are you? (idea, started, already selling — since when and how much)
stage.example: e.g. Company registered in 2026, selling at markets since May, about 3 000 € a month.

competitors.label: Who are your main competitors? Name them and what they offer.
competitors.example: e.g. Café A (200 m away, higher prices), bakery chain B (no lunch).

advantage.label: Why will customers choose you instead of them?
advantage.example: e.g. Lower lunch price, faster service, home-made pastries.

marketSize.label: How big is your market? (area, number of possible customers, trends)
marketSize.example: e.g. About 6 000 students and 1 500 office workers within 500 m.

who.label: Who are your customers? (people or companies, age, location)
who.example: e.g. Students 19–25 and office workers nearby; small companies for catering.

howMany.label: How many customers do you expect, and how often do they buy?
howMany.example: e.g. 120 customers a day, average purchase 7 €.

existing.label: Do you already have customers, orders, letters of intent or agreements?
existing.example: e.g. Catering agreement with company C for 40 lunches a week.

people.label: Who are the owners and key people? Their experience and education related to this business.
people.example: e.g. Mari (owner): 6 years as café manager; Jaan: trained chef.

roles.label: Who does what? Are there gaps you will fill? (accountant, new staff, partners)
roles.example: e.g. Mari runs the café and sales; accounting bought from an accounting firm.

channels.label: How will customers find out about you? Channels and budget.
channels.example: e.g. Instagram, student newspaper, flyers; 300 € a month.

prices.label: What are your prices and how did you set them?
prices.example: e.g. Lunch 6.50 €, 10% below Café A; coffee 2.80 €.

salesProcess.label: How do you sell? (shop, online, direct sales, partners)
salesProcess.example: e.g. In the café, online pre-orders, delivery through Wolt.

location.label: Where will you work? Premises, size, rent or own.
location.example: e.g. 80 m² ground-floor premises, 5-year lease, 1 200 € a month.

suppliers.label: Main equipment, suppliers and partners.
suppliers.example: e.g. Espresso machine (to buy), food from supplier D, coffee beans from roastery E.

permits.label: Licences, permits or registrations you need, and their status.
permits.example: e.g. Food business notice to the Agriculture and Food Board — submitted.

risks.label: What could go wrong? List the main risks.
risks.example: e.g. Fewer customers in summer; rent increase; the owner falls ill.

mitigation.label: How will you reduce each risk or react if it happens?
mitigation.example: e.g. Summer catering and terrace; lease price fixed for 3 years; trained second barista.

use.label: What exactly will the loan be used for? List items and amounts.

amountTerm.label: How much do you want to borrow and for how long?

repayment.label: How will you pay the loan back? From which income?
repayment.example: e.g. From café profit; monthly payment about 500 €, profit about 1 500 € a month.

amount.label: How much of your own money or assets do you put into the project?
amount.example: e.g. 8 000 € in money and kitchen equipment worth 3 000 €.

source.label: Where does your own money come from?
source.example: e.g. Personal savings; part from selling a car.

security.label: What can you offer as security for the loan?
security.example: e.g. Personal guarantee of the owner; the café equipment as a commercial pledge.

eisGuarantee.label: Would you like to use an EIS loan guarantee? (it can replace missing collateral)
eisGuarantee.example: e.g. Yes, we lack real estate to pledge.

existingDebts.label: Existing loans, leases or debts of the business and owners.
existingDebts.example: e.g. Car lease 250 € a month until 2028; no tax debts.

review.title: Bank officer check
review.intro: See your plan through a bank's eyes: a readiness score, the weak points, and the 10 hardest questions a credit officer would ask.
review.scoreNote: This score is an estimate made by this app. Only the bank decides on a loan.
review.checksIntro: The app compares your plan with what Estonian banks and EIS usually look for.

numbers.title: Sales and loan in the calculator
numbers.ok: The sales forecast and the loan are entered.
numbers.missing: Enter your sales forecast and the loan you are asking for.

dscr.title: Can the business pay the loan? (DSCR)
dscr.text: Lowest debt service coverage in the forecast: {value}. Banks usually want at least {minimum}.

cash.title: Money never runs out
cash.ok: The bank balance stays above zero in all 36 months. Lowest balance: {lowest}.
cash.fail: The bank balance falls below zero in {month} (lowest {lowest}). Add own money, choose a longer loan term or interest-only months, or cut early costs.

ownContribution.title: Own money in the project
ownContribution.text: Your own money is {share} of own money plus the loan. Banks often ask for {good}; {minimum} is the usual minimum.

equity.title: Equity share
equity.text: Lowest equity share of the balance sheet: {value}. Banks usually want at least {minimum}.

currentRatio.title: Short-term debts covered (current ratio)
currentRatio.text: Lowest current ratio: {value}. At least {minimum} is expected.
currentRatio.none: No short-term debts in the forecast.

debtToTurnover.title: Loan compared with yearly sales
debtToTurnover.text: Highest loan balance compared with yearly sales: {value}. At most {maximum} is recommended.
debtToTurnover.noSales: The forecast has a year without sales.

review.otherLanguage: This check is in {language}. Start a new check to get it in this language.
